the detection rate for neutron-star– black hole binaries with Advanced LIGOVirgo will decrease if the black hole angular momentum is not accounted for in gravitational-wave searches.

the precession of neutron-star–black-hole binaries will cause the gravitational-wave signal emitted by the system to deviate from the nonprecessing waveform models used in current gravitational-wave searches.

In summary, our research is concerned with

understanding the effects of the angular momentum of the neutron star and the black hole on the gravitational-wave signals emitted from neutron-star– black-holes inspiralling binaries and how this affects gravitational-wave searches.
improving the accuracy of the waveform models used to search for gravitational waves emitted by merging neutron-star– black- hole binaries.
the development of a search pipeline that can detect gravitational-wave signals from neutron-star– black hole binaries with the Advanced LIGO and Virgo detectors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
neglecting the precession of neutron star black hole binaries in the analysis of Advanced LIGO and Virgo data would lead to a reduction in the detection rate by 26% to 37%.
the detection rate for neutron-star– black hole binaries will be reduced by 25%–35% if the effect of black hole precession is neglected.

the detection of (10+ 1.4) M⊙ neutron-star – black-hole systems will be possible, but that the detection rate will be reduced by a few tens of percent if the effect of precessional motion is ignored in the search.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the effect of the angular momentum of the neutron-star– black- hole binary components on the emitted gravitational-wave signals should be included in the filter waveforms that are used to perform gravitational-wave searches.
the detection rate is reduced by a factor of ∼2 for systems with isotropic black hole spin distributions, and by a factor of 2–3 for systems with aligned spins.
the effect of precessing black holes on gravitational-wave searches is not as significant as the effect of precesing neutron stars.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the angular momentum of the neutron-star– black- hole binary must be included in gravitational-wave searches if the detection efficiency is to be optimized.
neglecting the black hole’s spin in searches for neutron-star– black- hole binaries will result in an underestimation of the detection rate of these systems.
the effect of the angular momentum of the compact object on the dynamics of the binary system should be included in the filter waveforms used in searches for neutron-star– black hole binaries.
